children: Alphabet Inc. Class C (NASDAQ:GOOG) posted strong Q2 revenue growth led by Google Services while Berkshire boosted its stake to roughly 100M Class C shares, even as GOOG sells debt to fund AI, strikes cloud deals for Moonshot AI, faces antitrust rulings and consumer award risks, and expands clean-energy buys.
Previous Week Recap
Berkshire Buys Alphabet Class C
: Berkshire now holds ~100M Alphabet Class C (GOOG) shares, ~106M combined A/C, valued ~$35–36.6B. Berkshire bought ~$10B this spring (6.5% discount) and added $17B in Q2.
GOOG Q2 Revenue Growth
: Alphabet Class C (GOOG) Q2 revenue $119.8B, +24% YoY. Google Services drove $94.5B. Advertising and services were main profit contributors, boosting top-line growth and revenue mix.
GOOG Taps Debt Markets
: GOOG sold multibillion-dollar debt to fund AI growth, joining peers tapping credit markets to finance AI investments; debt size and timing may affect shares and yield dynamics for traders.
AdX Divestiture Blocked
: Judge declined AdX divestiture, ordered interoperability fixes. Final order due in ~30 days. GOOG jumped ~1% to about $338.51 on the ruling.
Moonshot Kimi K3 On Cloud
: Alphabet (GOOG) is in talks to host Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 model on Google Cloud under a revenue-sharing deal; discussions reportedly include other major cloud providers and partners.
DOJ Antitrust Ruling Denied
: Court denied DOJ bid to break up Google small-business ad tools. Alphabet Class C (GOOG) shares tied to antitrust suit over its local advertising and customer-acquisition services.
Cape Station Geothermal Deal
: GOOG affiliate Google signed a 396 MW power purchase for Cape Station geothermal in Utah, delivery from 2028; option to expand ~600 MW, potential ~1 GW by June 2030, pending approvals.
Gemini 3.8 Flash Preview
: GOOG: Google plans Gemini 3.8 Flash release this week; internal tests show the Flash model yields faster responses and lower compute costs versus larger models, per Jetski comparisons.
West Virginia Solar Project
: GOOG backs West Virginia project: 86 MW solar, 10 MW/100 MWh zinc long-duration storage, 70 MW/280 MWh lithium storage for PJM. Solar online 2028; storage phased 2029–2030. GOOG will buy output.
Post-Opt-Out Data Suit
: GOOG faces a nearly $425M jury award to ~98–100M consumers over alleged post‑opt‑out data collection. Google plans to appeal; court approved $147M in plaintiffs’ attorneys’ fees.
This is an AI-generated summary and may contain inaccuracies. Please verify any important information with the original sources.
